# SMIOTA vs. ButterflyMX: Why You Shouldn't Trust Package Management to a Building Access Company

ButterflyMX recently reviewed SMIOTA's package lockers. The review has a significant flaw: it was written by a company that sells video intercoms — not package management systems.

Smiota Team
·
June 2026
·
8 min read
Body

ButterflyMX recently published a review of SMIOTA's package locker system. It's worth reading — not because it's accurate, but because it reveals something important about how ButterflyMX thinks about package management.

ButterflyMX is a video intercom and building access company. Their core product is a smartphone-based intercom that lets residents buzz in guests remotely. Their "package room" is an extension of that access control infrastructure — a room you unlock with a PIN — not a purpose-built package management solution.

SMIOTA does one thing: package management. That distinction is the foundation of everything that follows.

Pull quote

> "We believe package lockers are a state-of-the-art amenity that will provide a true benefit to our residents."
— VP, LIVEbe Communities

## ButterflyMX's Core Business Is Building Access — Not Package Management

ButterflyMX makes video intercoms. That's where they started, where their engineering focus lives, and what they're known for in the multifamily industry. Their package room is a feature add-on to that access control infrastructure, not a ground-up package management system.

That distinction shows up in the product:

- No smart locker option. Every delivery — a small envelope and a 60-pound box alike — goes into the same shared room.
- No per-package tracking. Their system logs who entered the room, not which package was delivered or picked up.
- No package-level resident notifications. Residents know someone entered the room — not that their specific package arrived.
- No package management platform. No dashboard for delivery volume, package aging, or resident pickup trends.

This isn't a criticism of ButterflyMX's intercom product. It's a recognition that package management is not their specialty — and it shows.

## SMIOTA Offers What ButterflyMX Can't: SmartLocker + PackageRoom on One Platform

SMIOTA doesn't ask property managers to choose between a smart locker and a package room. We offer both — managed from a single unified platform.

Feature cards

SmartLocker

### Individual Package Security

Each package gets its own secure compartment. Residents receive an instant notification with a unique pickup code. No shared access, no mix-ups, no theft risk. Every transaction logged at the package level.

PackageRoom

### Any Package, Any Size

For oversized items, furniture, bulk deliveries, and high-volume days. Couriers access through building security or outdoor configurations. Every drop-off is logged. Residents are notified immediately.

Unified Platform

### One Dashboard, Everything

Both systems run on the same platform. One admin dashboard, one resident app, one source of truth for every delivery and pickup across both the SmartLocker and PackageRoom.

## The Package Room Limitation ButterflyMX Doesn't Mention

A package room — regardless of who makes it — has one inherent limitation: shared access means shared risk.

When any resident with an access code can walk into a room containing everyone's packages, you've built a system that relies on resident honesty rather than package security. ButterflyMX's wide-angle camera captures who entered the room. It doesn't prevent someone from picking up the wrong package — or the right package that isn't theirs.

Smart lockers eliminate this entirely. This matters especially for:

- High-density urban buildings where package volume and resident turnover are high
- Luxury properties where residents have elevated expectations around security and service
- Garden-style communities where a single shared room can't serve residents spread across multiple buildings

## Responding to ButterflyMX's Specific Claims

Claim: "Couriers find SMIOTA complicated."

SMIOTA's SmartLocker interaction takes about 15 seconds. For couriers who prefer open drop-off, SMIOTA's PackageRoom is available on the same property. Properties get both options. The "complexity" ButterflyMX describes is the absence of any managed process — not a better one.

Claim: "SMIOTA can't handle oversized packages."

This is only true if you ignore SMIOTA's PackageRoom — which ButterflyMX's review does entirely. SMIOTA's combined solution handles standard parcels, refrigerated deliveries, and oversized items. The review evaluated a locker-only configuration and called it a verdict on SMIOTA. It isn't.

Claim: "SMIOTA lacks secure courier building entry."

Building access configurations depend on the property. SMIOTA works with existing building security infrastructure. Properties with outdoor locker installations require no building entry at all. This is deployment flexibility — not a product gap.

## The Real Question for Property Managers

When evaluating a package management system, the right question isn't "lockers or package room?" It's: is this vendor's primary expertise actually package management?

ButterflyMX's primary product is a video intercom. Package management is an add-on. SMIOTA's entire platform — every engineering decision, every product feature, every integration — is built around getting packages from courier to resident as securely and efficiently as possible.

That specialization is why properties like LIVEbe Communities choose SMIOTA. "We believe package lockers are a state-of-the-art amenity that will provide a true benefit to our residents." That's not a statement about a shared room with a PIN pad. That's a statement about a purpose-built package management platform that treats deliveries as a premium resident experience — not an afterthought.

Comparison table

## SMIOTA vs. ButterflyMX: Side by Side

| Feature | SMIOTA | ButterflyMX |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary product | Package management platform | Video intercom / building access |
| SmartLocker | ✓ Yes | ✗ No |
| PackageRoom | ✓ Yes | ✓ Yes |
| SmartLocker + PackageRoom combo | ✓ Yes | ✗ No |
| Per-package tracking | ✓ Yes | ✗ No (door-level only) |
| Individual resident notifications | ✓ Per delivery | ~ Room entry only |
| Unified admin dashboard | ✓ Yes | ✗ No |
| Purpose-built for package management | ✓ Yes | ✗ No |

## The Bottom Line

ButterflyMX makes a good intercom. If you need a video intercom system and want a basic package drop-off room as part of it, they're worth evaluating for that purpose.

If you're looking for a dedicated multifamily package management platform — one that offers individual parcel security, oversized package handling, a distributed locker model for garden-style properties, and a unified system that gives both residents and property managers full visibility — that's not what ButterflyMX sells.

That's what SMIOTA sells. And we've built nothing else.

Today's shoppers expect fast, flexible, reliable fulfillment. Smiota's smart lockers unify pickup, delivery, and returns into a secure, automated, 24/7 self-service experience — reducing operational friction while building customer trust and loyalty.

WHY
Why smart lockers for retail

## Enhance customer experience while optimizing operations.

Failed deliveries, queues at the counter, porch piracy, and slow returns all erode margin and loyalty. Smart lockers fix each one.

1

### Reduce failed deliveries & last-mile costs

Missed home deliveries and reattempts hurt margins and satisfaction. Lockers consolidate orders into secure pickup points — in stores, outdoors, or across locker networks.

2

### Enable 24/7 pickup convenience

Shoppers want control, not queues. Lockers allow anytime pickup — before work, after hours, or on weekends — so customers collect on their schedule.

3

### Prevent theft & secure high-value orders

Porch piracy and open pickup counters put orders at risk. Access-controlled, monitored compartments ensure only verified customers retrieve their purchases.

4

### Simplify returns with self-service drop-off

Returns don't need to slow operations. Lockers enable quick, contactless returns while automatically updating reverse-logistics workflows.

Integrate lockers into BOPIS and click-and-collect workflows to eliminate lines, speed handovers, and reduce staff involvement.

Hygienic, self-service pickup at stores, urban hubs, residential locations, or partner sites — ideal for omnichannel retail.

### Intelligent locker management

A cloud dashboard provides real-time tracking, automated notifications, access control, and complete audit trails for pickups and returns.

Turn store inventory into a last-mile asset. Serve same-day local pickup for e-commerce orders 24/7, including after store hours.

FAQ
FAQ

## Retail smart lockers, answered.

### How do smart lockers improve BOPIS (buy online, pick up in store) operations?

Smiota lockers replace attended pickup counters with self-service stations. Staff load the order into an assigned compartment and the customer receives a pickup code instantly. Customers collect at any time without queuing or waiting for staff — reducing friction for the customer and labor for the store.

### Can Smiota lockers handle online order returns in retail?

Yes. Customers drop returns into a designated return compartment and receive a confirmation. Store staff process returned items on their schedule — no need to staff a returns counter in real time. The return event is logged automatically for reporting.

### How are customers notified when their click-and-collect order is ready?

Customers receive an instant SMS or email notification with a secure PIN or QR code when their order is loaded into the locker. Pickup takes seconds — they scan the code or enter the PIN and the compartment opens. No app download required.

### What happens if a customer does not pick up their retail order?

Automated reminders are sent at store-configured intervals. If the order remains uncollected after a defined period, staff are notified through the admin dashboard and can return the item to stock or follow the store's standard unclaimed-order protocol.

### Can Smiota lockers turn a retail store into a micro-fulfillment hub?

Yes. Retailers use Smiota outdoor and in-store lockers to serve same-day local pickup for e-commerce orders, turning store inventory into a last-mile fulfillment asset. Carriers deposit directly, customers pick up 24/7 — including after store hours.

### Do Smiota retail lockers integrate with existing POS or OMS systems?

Smiota's open REST API connects with order management and POS platforms to trigger locker assignments automatically when an order is ready for pickup. Contact our team to confirm integration compatibility with your specific platform.

# Smiota Privacy Notice

Last modified: June 16, 2020

Welcome to Smiota Inc’s. (hereinafter referred to as “Smiota”, “Company”, “we”, “us”, “our”) privacy notice (the “Privacy Notice”).

Smiota respects your privacy and is committed to protecting your personal data.  This Privacy Notice will inform you as to how we look after your personal data when you use our Smiota locker products, website, or software applications in connection Smiota services and other goods or services managed by Smiota, Inc. (collectively our “Products”).

1. PRIVACY NOTICE PURPOSE:

- The purpose of this Privacy Notice is to notify you of the types of information we may collect through your use of our Products or through our clients as a step in our process to deploy our Products for your use.  This Privacy Notice will also inform you of how we use your information, your options to control communications and security procedures we use to protect your information.

1. CONTACT DETAILS:

- If you have any questions or comments about this notice, the ways in which Smiota collects and uses your information described here, your choices and rights regarding such use, or wish to exercise your rights under California law, please do not hesitate to contact us at [email protected].

1. CHANGES TO THE PRIVACY NOTICE

- This Privacy Notice version was last updated on June 16, 2020.

1. THE CATEGORIES OF DATA WE COLLECT

Personal information, personal data, or personally-identifiable information (PII) refers to information that identifies, relates to, describes, references, is reasonably capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular consumer, household, or device (hereinafter referred to as “personal information”, “personal data” or “personally-identifiable information”).  Personal data does not include anonymous data or deidentified information where your identity has been removed.  In particular, we have collected, used, stored, and/or transferred the following categories of personal information from our consumers within the last twelve (12) months:

| Category | Examples | Collected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Identifiers | A real name, alias, postal address, unique personal identifier,
online identifier, IP address, email address, account name,
package tracking number, or other similar identifiers. | YES |
| B. Personal information categories listed in the California
Customer Records statute | A name, signature, address, telephone number, employment. | YES |
| C. Protected classification characteristics | ADA data. | YES |
| D. Commercial information | Records of package label data. | YES |
| E. Biometric information | Genetic, physiological, behavioral, and biological characteristics
such as fingerprints, faceprints, voiceprints, or retina scans. | NO |
| F. Internet or other similar network activity | Browsing history, search history, package history, interaction
with a website or advertisement. | YES |
| G. Geolocation data | Physical location or movements. | YES |
| H. Sensory data | Audio, electronic, visual, thermal, or similar information. | NO |
| I. Professional or employment-related information | Current or past job history or performance evaluations. | NO |
| J. Non-public education information | Education records such as grades, transcripts, schedules,
student identification codes. | NO |
| K. Inferences drawn from other personal information | Profile reflecting preferences, behavior, attitudes, abilities. | NO |

# Information Security Policy

## Purpose

The Information Security Policy aims to establish an effective and elaborate information security management framework to manage the implementation of information security within Smiota.

## Scope

This policy applies to all organizational aspects of Smiota and all parties, its affiliated partners or subsidiaries, including data processing and process control systems, that are in possession of, or using information and/or facilities owned by Smiota.

This policy applies to all staff/ users that are directly or indirectly employed by Smiota, its subsidiaries or any entity conducting work on behalf of Smiota that involves the use of information assets owned by Smiota.

## Policy Enforcement and Compliance

Compliance with this policy is mandatory and organizational managers shall ensure continuous compliance monitoring within their departments. Compliance with the statements in this policy is a matter of annual review by the management. Any violation will result in disciplinary action by the ISMS Steering Committee.

Disciplinary action taken will depend on the severity of the violation which will be determined by the investigation. Actions such as termination or others as deemed appropriate by Smiota’s Management and can escalate to the ISMS Steering Committee.

## Waiver Criteria

This policy is intended to address information security requirements. If needed, waivers can be formally submitted to the infrastructure, including justification and benefits attributed to the waiver.

## Related Policies

- Logical Security Policy
- ISMS Management Policy
- Information Management & Classification Policy
- Clear Desk and Clear Screen Policy
- Mobile Device & Teleworking Policy
- Supplier Security Policy

## Document Owner

- ISMR

## Policy Management

Technological advances and changes in business requirements will necessitate periodic revisions to policies. Therefore, this policy may be updated to reflect changes or define new or improved requirements.

Deficiencies within this policy shall be immediately communicated to the ISMR. Policy changes will require the approval of the Management during Management Review Meetings. The Change Log shall be kept current and will be updated as soon as any change has been made.

## Information Security Policy

Management of Smiota is committed to protect its information assets by deploying information security controls that minimize the impact of any security incidents.

To create, maintain and continually improve the Information Security Management System and to achieve this objective, Smiota ensure the following:

- All applicable legal and contractual requirements are fulfilled.
- Confidentiality and integrity of information is maintained through a systematic process.
- Business continuity plans (DR site) will be established, maintained and tested.
- Risks to all corporate assets (tangible/intangible and human) are assessed and against all risks appropriate controls are implemented, and mitigation and contingency plans are defined.
- All corporate assets (tangible / intangible, and people) have a secure and safe environment.
- Conducive work environment has been provided to human resources, free from accidental and occupational hazards.
- All personnel are trained in information security practices, roles and responsibilities.

How it works

## Self-service in three steps — no assigned locker, no key to lose.

Day-use lockers are shared and on-demand. The system hands each person any open, right-sized locker, then frees it the moment they leave.

1

### Tap your badge

An RFID badge your people already carry identifies them at the locker — no app to download, no new credential to issue.

2

### Store or grab — instantly

An open locker opens automatically. Deposit a bag, laptop, or gear and go. One-click pickup when they return.

3

### Auto-freed for the next person

When the item's collected, the locker returns to the pool. Multiple people deposit and pick up at the same time.

### Transit & public venues

Self-service bag and gear storage that can generate rental revenue.

Enterprise-grade & low-maintenance

## Secure by design, and built to run for years untouched.

🔒

### SOC 2 Type II & ISO 27001

Certified cloud platform with encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, and full audit logging.

🔌

### 120V AC power & Ethernet/Wi-Fi

☎️

Always-on support and proactive monitoring keep every unit online and in service.

FAQ
FAQ

## Day-use smart lockers, answered.

### How do day-use lockers differ from assigned lockers?

Day-use lockers aren't tied to one person. The system hands each user any open, right-sized locker for their visit, then returns it to the shared pool when they leave — so a bank of lockers serves far more people than permanently-assigned units.

### How do people open a locker?

They tap the RFID badge they already carry. Smiota also supports mobile app, PIN, and QR access — no new credential required for members or employees.

### Can several people use the lockers at the same time?

Yes. Smiota day-use lockers support concurrent access, so multiple people can deposit and pick up at once without waiting at a single screen.

### Do the lockers need to be wired for power?

Yes. Each locker bank connects to a standard 120V power outlet and the internet (wired or Wi-Fi). The individual electronic locks are battery-powered, so you don't wire every door — but the unit itself needs power and a network connection.

### What systems do they integrate with?

Smiota integrates with access-control and membership platforms including HID Global, Brivo, Mindbody, Club Automation, and Jonas Club Software, plus SSO and an open API for custom integrations.

### Is it secure?

Yes. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, with encryption, role-based access, full audit logging, and 24/7 monitoring and support.

Smart lockers replace manual package logging and employee notification workflows. Carriers deposit packages into assigned compartments using a universal carrier access code. Employees receive an instant notification with a secure PIN or QR code and collect their package at any time — without visiting the front desk or mailroom.

Smiota integrates with HID Global, Lenel S2, Okta, Microsoft Azure AD, Allegion ENGAGE, and SAML 2.0-compatible identity providers. Employees use existing badge or SSO credentials — no separate locker accounts required.

### Can Smiota lockers be managed across multiple office locations?

Yes. Smiota's centralized admin dashboard gives IT and facilities teams visibility and control across all locations from a single login. Site-level configurations, user group permissions, and real-time utilization data are accessible from any device.

## Campus smart lockers, answered.

### What types of smart lockers does Smiota offer for universities?

Smiota offers package lockers, IT device lockers, library book lockers, day-use lockers, and weatherproof outdoor lockers — all manageable from a single platform to support 24/7 campus access across multiple departments.

### Can Smiota lockers integrate with campus ID systems?

Yes. Smiota supports integration with student ID cards, RFID badges, and mobile credentials so students and staff can access lockers using existing campus credentials — no separate logins or PIN codes required.

### How do students get notified when a package arrives?

Students receive instant SMS, email, or app push notifications with a secure PIN or QR code. Pickup takes seconds — no front desk visit or staff interaction needed.

### Can lockers be installed outdoors on campus?

Yes. Smiota's weatherproof outdoor lockers can be installed in quads, near residence halls, transit hubs, and building entrances to support true 24/7 access even outside of building hours.

Automated reminders are sent via SMS and email. If the item remains uncollected, it follows campus-defined escalation rules configured in the admin dashboard — such as returning the item to the mailroom after a set period.

### Does Smiota support multi-building or multi-campus deployments?

Yes. Smiota's platform is built to scale across multiple buildings, departments, and campuses. Administrators get centralized visibility and control from a single dashboard while each location operates independently.

### Can lockers be used for IT device lending and returns?

Yes. IT departments can use Smiota lockers to manage laptops, tablets, chargers, projectors, and repaired equipment with full audit trails, automated check-in/out, and real-time availability tracking.

### Are Smiota lockers ADA compliant?

Locker banks can be configured to meet ADA accessibility requirements, including appropriate reach ranges and accessible interface heights, ensuring all students including those with disabilities can use the system independently.

# Smart Locker Comparison: Smiota vs Luxer One vs Quadient vs Velocity

Researching package locker systems takes time. We've built this honest breakdown to help facilities managers, IT directors, and property operators evaluate the real differences in pricing, integrations, hardware, and deployment flexibility.

See Smiota in action

## Feature comparison at a glance

## Vendor profiles

A quick summary of each vendor's strengths, weaknesses, and the buyer profiles they serve best.

Smiota

### Best for: multi-use enterprise deployments

Smiota serves the widest range of use cases — package delivery, IT asset management, day-use personal storage, and library hold pickup — from a single platform. Strong ITSM and access control integrations make it the choice for corporate campuses, universities, and government facilities that need more than package delivery.

Strengths: broadest integration ecosystem, single-platform for all locker types, library-grade ILS support, outdoor-rated hardware.

Luxer One

### Best for: multifamily and large residential

Luxer One has deep penetration in the multifamily apartment market with strong PMS integrations for Yardi, RealPage, and Entrata. Good fit for property management companies that primarily need package delivery in residential buildings.

Weaknesses: limited use case breadth, no ITSM or library integrations, weaker support for corporate/enterprise buyers.

Velocity Smart

### Best for: basic package delivery

Velocity Smart provides solid entry-level package locker solutions for multifamily and commercial buildings. Limited integration depth makes it a better fit for simpler deployments without complex access control or ITSM requirements.

Weaknesses: minimal outdoor options, limited third-party integrations, less flexible for enterprise use cases.

Quadient

### Best for: postal/carrier-focused deployments

Quadient (formerly Neopost) has strong roots in postal and mail processing. Good for organizations focused on carrier-agnostic package acceptance. Limited software platform compared to newer entrants.

Weaknesses: aging platform, limited enterprise software integrations, heavier focus on hardware than software.

LockNCharge

### Best for: K-12 device management

LockNCharge specializes in device charging and storage for K-12 education. Strong for Chromebook and tablet management in schools. Not a general-purpose package locker and does not serve the commercial or enterprise market well.

Weaknesses: education-only focus, no package delivery use case, limited to device charging/storage.

## How to choose a smart locker system

Most buyer regret comes from selecting a system optimized for one use case and discovering it can't scale to others. Here's the framework we recommend.

### 1. List every use case — today AND in 18 months

Most properties start with package delivery and add IT asset exchange, day-use personal storage, or equipment lending within 18 months. Selecting a vendor that can handle all of these from day one prevents a costly replacement.

### 2. Map your integration requirements

What systems does the locker need to connect to? PMS, ITSM, access control, ILS, campus ID — each integration requirement eliminates vendors. Make this list before RFP, not after.

### 3. Clarify outdoor requirements up front

Not all "outdoor" lockers are built to the same spec. Ask for the IP rating, operating temperature range, and warranty for outdoor hardware. IP54 (dust-protected, splash-resistant) is the minimum for exposed installations.

### 4. Stress-test the software, not just the hardware

The hardware is a commodity. The platform — notifications, reporting, API, multi-site management, user roles — is what differentiates vendors after year one. Ask for a live demo of the admin dashboard, not just the locker door opening.

### 5. Ask about total cost of ownership

Get pricing for: hardware, installation, annual SaaS/service fees, integration fees, and support SLA tiers. Per-door pricing models look attractive initially but can become expensive at scale. Understand the 3-year TCO, not just the upfront cost.

### 6. Check support structure

Who handles hardware service? Vendor direct or third-party? What's the SLA for on-site service? What's the escalation path? Lockers are infrastructure — downtime has visible operational consequences.

## Common questions from smart locker buyers

### How much do smart lockers cost?

Smart locker pricing varies widely based on locker count, configuration, outdoor/indoor, and software features. Most enterprise deployments run $800–$2,500 per door for hardware, plus $500–$1,500/year per locker bank in SaaS/service fees. Smaller deployments (under 20 doors) typically have higher per-door costs. Request a quote from vendors with your specific unit count and use case for accurate pricing.

### What's the difference between Smiota and Luxer One?

Luxer One is primarily a multifamily package locker company with strong apartment PMS integrations. Smiota covers more use cases — including IT asset management, library hold pickup, day-use personal storage, and outdoor lockers — from a single platform. If your use case is purely package delivery in a residential building, Luxer One is a viable option. If you need integrations beyond PMS, or more than one type of locker use case, Smiota's platform breadth gives you more room to grow.

### Can smart lockers work without a cellular connection?

Most smart locker systems require either ethernet or cellular connectivity for real-time notifications and remote management. Some vendors support offline grace periods where previously-issued codes continue working without connectivity, but real-time features (notifications, admin dashboard, new code generation) require connectivity. Ask each vendor about their offline fallback behavior for your specific installation.

### How long does smart locker installation take?

Standard indoor locker installations typically take 1–3 days depending on unit count and site readiness. Outdoor installations or those requiring conduit runs can take 3–5 days. Software configuration and integration setup adds 2–4 weeks for complex ITSM or PMS integrations. Plan for a full pilot-to-production timeline of 6–16 weeks including procurement, installation, and user training.

Most libraries start with one branch and one use case (hold pickup or equipment lending), expand to additional use cases at that branch, then roll out to other branches. Implementation timeline is typically 8 to 16 weeks from contract to live, depending on site readiness and ILS integration scope.

### How do day-use smart lockers work at gyms and fitness centers?

Members claim a locker on arrival via mobile app, QR scan, or PIN. The locker is theirs for the session. When they leave, it auto-releases back to the available pool — no physical key, no staff reset required. Members interact with the locker independently, with no front desk involvement.

Lockers release automatically at the end of a session based on configurable time limits. If a member forgets to release, the locker auto-expires after the configured window and returns to the available pool. Administrators can override and release any compartment remotely from the cloud dashboard.

### Can Smiota lockers be assigned for specific classes or personal training sessions?

Yes. Administrators can pre-assign specific compartments to class participants or personal training clients. The locker activates for the session window and auto-releases when the session ends. This eliminates the need for physical key distribution for class-based storage.

Facility staff receive an alert for any locker that has not been released by closing time. Administrators can send a notification to the member via the platform and, if necessary, override the lock remotely — without needing a physical master key on-site.

## One Platform. Every Vertical. Every Workflow.

Smiota smart lockers are purpose-built for the environments where package and asset management is most complex — high-volume residential buildings, university campuses, public libraries, government facilities, hospital networks, and enterprise offices. Each deployment is configured for the specific workflows, integrations, and compliance requirements of its environment.

### Multifamily Residential

Apartment communities face surging delivery volume from carriers like USPS, UPS, FedEx, Amazon, and DHL. Smiota centralizes all deliveries into secure, self-service lockers accessible 24/7 — eliminating mailroom overflow, reducing staff workload, and giving residents a pickup experience that consistently ranks as a top amenity. Integrations with Yardi, Entrata, AppFolio, RealPage, and Buildium mean resident data stays in sync automatically.

### Universities and Campuses

Campus mailrooms and residence halls handle thousands of packages per week during the academic year, with surge conditions during move-in that overwhelm manual processes. Smiota integrates with campus credential systems including HID Global, CBORD, and Transact Campus so students use their existing ID cards or mobile credentials — no separate app required.

### Public and Academic Libraries

Libraries use Smiota lockers to offer 24/7 hold pickup and after-hours returns without additional staff. The platform integrates with major integrated library systems (ILS) including Koha, Ex Libris Alma, OCLC WorldShare, SirsiDynix Symphony, and Innovative Sierra — automating hold notifications, locker assignments, and return processing end to end.

### Enterprise and Government

For corporate mailrooms, government facilities, and healthcare institutions, Smiota provides access-controlled storage with full chain of custody, audit logging, and compliance-ready architecture. The platform meets SOC 2 and ISO 27001 standards, supports SSO via Azure AD, Okta, and Google Workspace, and deploys on Google Cloud, AWS, or Azure.

### Hardware Built for Real Environments

Smiota lockers are available in indoor, outdoor, day-use, asset management, and smart package room configurations — with multiple compartment sizes, UV-C sanitation options, antimicrobial surfaces, and temperature-controlled variants for grocery, pharmaceutical, and cold-chain deliveries. Every unit ships with ADA-accessible touchscreen interfaces and integrates with existing building access control and surveillance systems.
